profile.headline: Software Engineer
profile.summary: I am a passionate and creative individual who uses problem-solving and logic to continuously promote and encompass innovative thinking. I aspire to act as a role model to my underrepresented rural community in the California Central Valley and encourage the pursuit of higher education and work in the tech industry

positions.title: Software Engineer I
positions.description: Maintain a web platform that processes almost 500,000 loans a month. Work with customer feedback to enhance our product and keep customers satisfied. Learn new technologies to maintain scalability for more loan processing. Participate in employee groups focused on mentorship and career development.

positions.title: Cal NERDS Student Coordinator
positions.description: Managed all finances and payment processing. Developed a quick and maintainable order processing system using excel to decrease overall turn-around time. Processed over $50,000 worth of invoices and over $10,000 in both student and employee reimbursements. Worked on projects and planned events for program members with a team and individually.

positions.title: Berkeley Math Tournament - Problem Writer/Grader
positions.description: Problem writer for both the Berkeley Math Tournament (BMT) for high school students and the Berkeley mini Math Tournament(BMMT) for middle school students. I attended weekly meetings to write problems according to various grade standards and develop the tournament exams along with other problem writers. During the tournament, I helped grade over 100 exams for students with high accuracy. Through the program, I traveled to China as a tournament director and grader for the first Berkeley mini Math Tournament.

positions.title: Research Assistant
positions.locationName: Redwood Center for Theoretical and Computational Neuroscience
positions.description: Our goal was to understand auditory processing in the brain. By training a sparse coding algorithm on a broader set of stimuli, we found some regularities that are common to many classes of natural sounds as well as regularities that only appear in some sounds, including possibly some interesting structure that doesn’t occur in speech. We then compared what our model learns to measurements in the neuroscience literature of what neurons in the auditory system respond to, and/or predict measurements that have not yet been made, in order to better understand and explain the relevant areas of the auditory system and help guide experimental research efforts.

organizations.name: Lambda Theta Alpha Latin Sorority, Incorporated
organizations.description: As a sister of Lambda Theta Alpha Latin Sorority, Inc. Delta Omicron chapter I am involved in helping plan professional development and academic workshops for the Berkeley community. I've assisted in fundraising over $1,500 becoming the top national undergraduate chapter for St. Jude that also contributed to the organization’s national pool of over $50,000 for cancer research during the 2016-2017 school year. As fundraising chair, I organize monthly Pupusa Sales serving up to 1K people to fundraise for St. Jude research Hospital, our national philanthropy, and our semester scholarships for high school students.

organizations.name: New Experiences for Research and Diversity in Science (Cal NERDS) - UC Berkeley
organizations.description:
The Cal NERDS program encompasses 5 programs, Bergeron Scholars, MCAT Prep, NSF Bridge to the Doctorate, UC Leads, and NSF CAMP.  Cal NERDS as a program on campus promotes professional development opportunities for students, connects students with mentors, and outreach for the community. Each student belongs to one of the 5 programs. I am a member of the National Science Foundation California Alliance Minority Participation (NSF CAMP). The NSF CAMP program provides resources and mentors for students to conduct research during their undergrad career. With that, the opportunity to go to the annual statewide CAMP Symposium to present research. It also encourages students to continue with higher education and apply to graduate programs. 

Learn more about Cal NERDS here: calnerds.berkeley.edu
